quest.title: Sinister Undercurrent
quest.description: On an otherwise ordinary day on the road, you suddenly feel a strange discomfort...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x425, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: #How are you, {NICKNAME}? Feeling any better today?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Baizhu about your dream and the special helper you encountered.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: You were pulled into a mysterious space inside a dream and stabbed by a spike?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: I can't offer much about the spike, but there are many ancient texts that describe the phenomenon of being transported to a different world in dream.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: For example, "A Drunken Adeptal Dream" describes the story of a woodcutter whose soul was mistakenly pulled into another world and remained there for several years before making it back.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: If I'm not mistaken, there used to be a god whose power involved dreams and souls. But, I thought that god had died...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: #A god, hmm... Well, in any case, caution is the name of the game, I think. Take care of yourself, {NICKNAME}, and don't hesitate to contact us if you need help.

talks.objective: Look for Baizhu at Bubu Pharmacy
Meet Baizhu in the back room of the pharmacy

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You should get some rest. Paimon can tell how tired you are.

talks.objective: Meet Baizhu in the back room of the pharmacy

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Ah, looks like we have a special guest.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, welcome! What can I do for you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #It's {NICKNAME} — {M#he}{F#she} looks absolutely beat these days. {M#He}{F#She} has these huge dark circles around {M#his}{F#her} eyes, like {M#he}{F#she} hasn't slept a wink.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #And {M#he}{F#she} keeps spacing out! You have to call {M#his}{F#her} name several times before {M#he}{F#she} snaps out of it... What do you think it is? Is {M#he}{F#she} sick?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: #Oh? Is {NICKNAME} prone to sickness? I find this surprising.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Very peculiar... In all the time we've been acquainted, this is the first time you've come to me with a health complaint. Come, let me take a look at you.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, Paimon does not like that expression, Baizhu... It's not serious, is it?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Hmm, complexion is good, eyes are clear, breathing is steady, pulse is strong...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: #Physically, you appear to be in good condition, {NICKNAME}. In theory, your energy level should reflect that. You should be feeling right as rain.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And yet... I do feel like something is "off."

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Hence my concern. A clean bill of health is usually a good thing. But, in this case, it likely means your situation is more complicated.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Physical illnesses come with detectable symptoms that can be used to diagnose, medicate, and cure the condition. But afflictions of a non-physical nature... they fall outside a doctor's realm of expertise.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What do you mean, "non-physical nature"?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Curses, dark magic... It's hard to say. It could just as easily be a simple case of mental fatigue.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Why don't you rest here for a bit? Whatever it is we're dealing with, clues to your condition are sure to reveal themselves in time. Once we know the root cause, we can administer the right treatment.

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: I've seen my fair share of mental afflictions. To start with, some calming incense, a good night's sleep, and a good meal will do you a world of good.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: In the meantime, Changsheng and I will review the relevant literature for afflictions that present with mental fatigue.

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: *sigh*... Still, we're not experts on this kind of thing. I say, we should strongly consider calling in a specialist as soon as possible.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... Must be a rare condition if not even Baizhu and Changsheng have seen it before...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, all we can do is take their advice. You look like you're about to collapse, anyway.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just get some rest. Paimon will be right here by your side! Fingers crossed you'll be all better when you wake up!

talks.objective: Take a rest in the back room of the pharmacy
Take a rest in the back room of the pharmacy

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Where am I?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (There's a thick fog covering my field of vision.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This feels more real than a dream, but too chilling to be real life. My breath freezes in my throat before I can even exhale it... It feels like my soul has been wrenched from my body and thrust into this strange and unfamiliar space.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Whichever direction I look in, there's no end in sight. And worse than that... I think there's something in the fog, following me like a shadow.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If this is a dream, how long till I wake up? And if it's not, then where in the world am I?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oof...!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What in the... Something just pierced through the fog and stabbed me in the back. But, there's no blood...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (There's a strange light coming from the wound, and I see this familiar-looking spike retreating back into the darkness... Deep inside, it feels like a part of me is missing. And now another wave of fatigue is washing over me...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Rise and shine! Time to wake up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn*... For once, you're making Paimon look like an early riser. It's already afternoon! Hopefully all that sleep did you some good. Feeling any better?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A cut? What, did you scratch yourself in your sleep? Alright, let Paimon take a look...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Nope! Nothing there... *gasp* Wait, did you have a nightmare?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Okay, don't panic, umm... Paimon heard that dreams tell us what we need by showing us the opposite, so... if you had a nightmare, maybe all you need is something to cheer you up! C'mon, Paimon will treat you to something yummy!

choices.text: I need you to check if there's a cut on my back...

talks.objective: Go have a meal with Paimon
Go have a meal with Paimon

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You and Paimon head to Wanmin Restaurant. Sensing that something isn't right, Paimon orders a bunch of dishes to cheer you up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? So in this dream, you were trapped in a weird place with thick fog everywhere, and then a spike came out of nowhere and stabbed you in the back?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, well that's a new one. Are you sure it was a dream? 'Cause from the way you describe it, it sounds like you were really there...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, then again, you woke up right where you went to bed. And you were definitely in a deep sleep this morning.

choices.text: I don't know what to make of it, either...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then, it's decided. Paimon will stay up and watch over you tonight! If anyone tries to mess with you, Paimon will beat 'em up!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Or, uh... Wake you up first and then we can beat 'em up together!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Paimon's smile has a way of putting me at ease.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (But, what I saw is still bothering me. That dream was so chilling, and it almost feels like there's something watching me from some corner of the world even now...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Something stabbed me in my dream, but when I woke up, there was no wound. Still, if I focus on that area, I feel a vague aching... almost as if, deep underneath the flesh, something is...)
...Something is missing?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, did you just say something?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You heard that, too?
The flesh remains whole, but the soul is incomplete. Left unresolved, the mind will wither away along with it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wah, what the... Wait! Paimon remembers you! You're Childe's master! Sk... ork?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Skirk.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! What are you doing here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The last time we saw you was at the Primordial Sea in Fontaine, right? But, then we left and never learned where you went after that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Childe's been looking everywhere for you, by the way. What brings you to Wanmin Restaurant, of all places? You came here looking for us? And were you the one behind that hocus-pocus just now?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Tell me. What is it that you saw?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Tight-lipped, huh? I suppose that's fair.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: You. I'll take a glass of wine.

response.speaker: Chef Mao
response.text: Hmm? Oh, of course. Coming right up.

response.speaker: Chef Mao
response.text: We make this one in-house — it's not too strong. Enjoy!

response.speaker: Captain Wu
response.text: Chef Mao, I'll take a Grilled Tiger Fish over here!

response.speaker: Chef Mao
response.text: Coming right up! *sigh*... If I knew we'd be this busy, I wouldn't have approved Shenhe's vacation...

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: At the end of the day, what happens to you is of little consequence to me. I'm not here to try and win you over. Trust me or not — the choice is yours.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: If you want my help, now's the time to speak up. You have until I finish my drink.

choices.text: What do you know about this situation?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I was investigating an Abyssal disturbance in the area and happened to notice you.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Part of your soul is damaged, and the wound bears traces of Abyssal corrosion. Need I say more?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Neither of those things sound good...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Skirk seems to know something. And given what I've seen of her strength, I bet she can tell what happened to me.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I don't know what her goal is, but in this moment at least, I don't think she has bad intentions.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well? Should we trust her?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What do you think, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She mentioned an Abyssal disturbance... Maybe that has something to do with what's going on with you. But, we could always find a different expert on the Abyss to help us out...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Not on short notice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, and that thing she said about your soul being damaged is scaring Paimon... Definitely something we should fix sooner rather than later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Skirk's an interesting one, that's for sure. But from what Childe's told us, she doesn't seem... evil, at least.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Well? Have you made up your mind?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What I saw was a dark space shrouded in a dense fog that wouldn't disperse.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You give Skirk a brief description of your "dream."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, that's all we know, Miss Skirk, um, ma'am. Can you help us?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: So, you couldn't disperse the fog...

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: ...I understand. Come find me in the Guili Plains when you're done here. Oh, and I left cash for the drink on the table. Settle the bill for me, will you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, uh, okay... Huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She disappeared!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You and Paimon quickly finish your meal and go to settle the bill.

response.speaker: Chef Mao
response.text: Wait, hold on, you overpaid. Here's your change.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, no, this includes the drink, so it should be the right amount.

response.speaker: Chef Mao
response.text: I didn't think you two ordered a drink.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We didn't! It was that lady who came and sat with us, remember? You brought it out to her yourself!

response.speaker: Chef Mao
response.text: You sure? I could have sworn there were only two of you at that table...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What?

response.speaker: Captain Wu
response.text: Haha, what did you put in their dish, Chef Mao? Some kind of hallucinogenic mushroom? You've got them seeing things!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seeing things? Wait, so neither of you noticed her? Young lady, about this tall, wearing a purple dress? She ordered a glass of wine.

response.speaker: Chef Mao
response.text: Ohh... Now you mention it, that vaguely rings a bell. And it looks like I did open the wine jar, so... Haha, it must have just slipped my mind. In any case, that settles your bill. Come again soon!

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Chef Mao, check please!

response.speaker: Chef Mao
response.text: Coming!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, what was going on there? It's like they didn't remember Skirk being there at all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even Paimon was half-convinced we hallucinated the whole thing... But, that Mora she left for us was definitely real.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh... This whole situation is giving Paimon the creeps... But anyway, she told us to head to the Guili Plains, right? Let's not keep her waiting!

choices.text: Maybe it was just a very lifelike dream.

talks.objective: Go to Guili Plains to investigate

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, what are all these Rifthounds doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, looks like they're collecting something...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go check it out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, this is what they were collecting. It looks kinda like...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: God remains?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! What is going on here...

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: From the moment they are born, all beings with great power have an impact on this world. Even if their body is sundered and their soul extinguished, their influence remains.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Gods are the most common example of that. The remnants of gods who fell thousands of years ago remain buried deep within the earth, carrying within them a warped will and a dark curse.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Together, these remnants form what you call "god remains." And it appears that some of those sealed here were dug up and removed. There are traces left, but they're fading fast.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: ...What are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: N—Nothing! Just wanted to make sure you were, um, real...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #She's definitely not a ghost, {NICKNAME}. Paimon poked her and she's solid...

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Your life hangs in the balance, and that's what you're fixated on? Strange set of priorities...

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: It was just a trick to avoid being perceived. If someone notices me, those memories are erased, simple as that.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Unlike you, I have no desire to establish a connection with the world. The weak and the lowly have no right to remember me. They're lucky they only have a few missing memories to show for it.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Now, can we please get back on track?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay! Um, where were we...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, the god remains! So basically, there's now less of them here than there used to be, right? Isn't that a good thing?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In our experience, god remains are one-hundred percent bad news. A lot of terrible things have happened because of them!

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Maybe it's a good thing by human standards. But, power doesn't come from nothing, and it doesn't just disappear for no reason.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: The remains aren't just gone — they were taken.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Like part of my soul was taken?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: #Very clever, {NICKNAME}. You aren't the only one who had something taken from you. There are victims like you everywhere — the only difference being, you can speak, and the remains cannot. So, it went unnoticed.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Something similar happened in Sumeru. Within the span of one night, countless Consecrated Beasts were slaughtered, and a large amount of the god remains buried in the desert went missing.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Of course, god remains are just one of the targets. The culprit is chipping away at sources of power all over this world, including the Stella Fortuna above.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, you mean... the stars?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Mm-hmm. Forty-two of them have died out in the past few months alone.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: In Khaenri'ah, people believed that powerful individuals have corresponding Stella Fortuna. Even should that individual fall, their Stella Fortuna would not disappear, but gradually evolve into a new constellation.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Yet now, stars are disappearing from the skies entirely, and it's not hard to deduce what's happening to the power they contain.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Something has been leeching power from this world like a parasite steals nutrients from a host. And, now, it's no longer satisfied with the remains of the dead — it wants you.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: This time, it only took a fragment of your soul. But next time? There's no telling how far it could go.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But, why me?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: No one knows. All I know for certain is this — getting back what you lost will not be easy.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Considering how much power this entity has stolen, it must be a god-level being by now at least. But, that's not the real concern. Souls are fragile things, and yours could easily be crushed if you go up against it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... So, you're gonna help us, right?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: We're going to help each other. You are my ticket to uncovering this thing's true identity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, great! You seem super strong, and you know a lot about the Abyss, so Paimon will take it!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Don't get all mushy on me. All I'm doing is helping you get back to normal after a sudden crisis.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: And, I should warn you, getting mixed up with me can have unforeseen consequences. We're on very different journeys. You don't want to be in my debt, trust me.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: You help me uncover the truth behind this entity, and I'll help you recover what you lost. This is a transaction, that's all.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: You would do well to remember that. Now, come along.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeesh... You'd think she'd be a little friendlier since she's agreed to help us. But nope, she's just like when we met her in the Primordial Sea... So cold...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, whatever! If that's how it's gonna be, then she doesn't deserve our friendship! What she does deserve is a super embarrassing nickname...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, Paimon's got it! "Frosty the Lavender Melon"! Hehe, serves that ice queen right.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, the important thing is that we get that piece of your soul back! So, let's follow her and see what sort of plan she's got!

choices.text: The other diners acted like you were never there.

talks.objective: Follow Skirk through the Abyssal rift

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, this place is way bigger than Paimon expected! Where are we?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: This is where I live. I suppose it's the closest thing I have to a "home" here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It seems more like somewhere in the Abyss?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: It is. I brought you here because time flows differently in this place.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: I don't know how much Ajax has told you, but when he fell into this space, I mentored him for three months. In that time, only three days passed in the outside world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ajax... Oh, right! That's Childe's real name. Yeah, Paimon remembers him mentioning something like that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, a month here is equivalent to one day in the outside world? That should mean we're safe from that power-hungry soul-snatcher for now, right?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: #Yes, well, I didn't bring you here just to show you around. In the outside world, {NICKNAME} could be attacked at any moment. But, coming here has bought us quite a bit of time.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Now, we just need to figure out how to investigate that place you saw. The one full of fog.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Both your description and the Abyssal disturbance I felt point to that space having some connection to the Abyss. It could even be a domain similar to this one.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: The thief who stole that fragment of your soul is hiding there. But the Abyss is a chaotic and turbulent place. If we want to pinpoint their location, we need to see what that space looks like without the fog.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Abyssal power can grant a special form of sight. Have you ever wielded Abyssal power before?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Okay, do you plan to learn?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: That tracks. All the information you have suggests the Abyss is something sinister, and that Abyssal power is a wild and dangerous force that always spells disaster.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And you're saying that's not true?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Depends on your perspective. Floods and hurricanes take countless lives too, but if one day you gained the power to control them, what was once a calamity is now just another tool in your arsenal.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I'll respect your opinion, though. Just means we have to turn to the second-best option.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's this?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: A little Abyss Crystal that contains my power. Wear it on your head, and we'll be able to perform dream-mirroring when we fall asleep.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ..."Dream-mirroring"?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: It means experiencing whatever the other person is dreaming. Everything they see, think, and feel.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Since you haven't studied the art of using Abyssal power and have no plans to jump in the deep end right now, I'll have to do the investigating for you.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: With dream-mirroring, every time you slip into a deep sleep, I'll see with my own eyes whatever scene plays out in your mind. Then, I can guide you through the dream environment and we'll take back what was stolen from you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... You make it sound so simple!

choices.text: So all I need to do is... wait?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Tough to say. This is an unprecedented situation for both of us. Even assuming we do manage to find where this entity is hiding, like I said, getting your soul fragment back won't be easy.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: To play it safe, I need to give you some special training first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Wait, you're gonna teach {NICKNAME} some of your martial arts?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Does that mean... the next time we see Childe, we have to treat him like our senior!?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Do as you want. For my part, I don't see you as my disciples.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: You're already a pretty good fighter. All I'm planning to do is build on your current skills and train you for the specific scenarios that I think we might face.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: But that's enough talk. If you're ready to do this, then come with me. Time might be more lenient here, but that's no excuse to waste it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She moves fast... Paimon can hardly keep up with her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, "special training," huh? Kind of a rare opportunity... With your skills, there's not a lot of people qualified to train you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The last time something like this happened was probably... "Anti-Raiden Shogun Training," right? Feels like a lifetime ago.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Skirk seems pretty strong too though. Remember how she said that the All-Devouring Narwhal was just her master's "pet"? Huh, maybe we really will learn something here!

choices.text: Is there anything you need me to do?
I'm kind of at odds with the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Geez! You're like "space out" city over there! What's up with you today?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Why does Paimon's voice sound so far away?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You feeling okay? Hmm... We've been traveling all over lately, so maybe you've come down with something... That's it — we're getting Baizhu to check you over.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, Baizhu isn't in his shop...

dialogues.speaker: Pedestrian at Pharmacy Entrance
dialogues.text: Oh, you're looking for Dr. Baizhu? He's resting today, but he said to send any patients to the back room.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, okay! Thanks! We'll head on through.
